executive_summary: Admin route group is protected by 4-layer middleware stack: `['installed', 'apiKey', 'auth:sanctum', 'localization', 'throttle:admin-mutation']`. The `apiKey` middleware is a SHARED-SECRET HEADER CHECK ONLY (not a role gate) — see app/Http/Middleware/ApiKeyMiddleware.php L23-28. `auth:sanctum` only verifies token validity, not role/ability. THE WHOLE AUTHORIZATION SURFACE depends on per-controller `permission:*` middleware. 71/87 (82%) admin controllers have it. 16 do not — 3 are dangerous, 13 are acceptable (route-level gating or pure self-service).

middleware_stack_breakdown.installed: App\Http\Middleware\Installed — guards Setup wizard. Pass-through after install.

apiKey.behavior: Reads `config('app.api_key')` (env API_KEY). Checks `X-Api-Key` header equality. Returns 400 invalid otherwise.
apiKey.verdict: NOT a permission gate. NOT a tenant gate. Any client knowing the SHARED secret passes. SEC-FIX commit migrated from env() to config() to survive config:cache (L20-21).

middleware_stack_breakdown.auth:sanctum: Verifies Bearer token + revoked status. No role/ability check at this layer.
middleware_stack_breakdown.throttle:admin-mutation: Rate limit on per-IP-per-route. Defense-in-depth, not authz.

acceptable_self_service: MenuController (catalog read-only, used by POS runtime)
AnalyticSectionController (mutations need check — see finding S-1)

findings.title: MyOrderDetailsController::orderDetails — IDOR within same branch
findings.evidence: app/Http/Controllers/Admin/MyOrderDetailsController.php has ZERO permission middleware. Route `/api/admin/my-order/show/{user}/{order}` (routes/api.php L574) binds both params freely. Inside OrderService::orderDetails (L1411-1422), the check is `$order->user_id == $user->id` — both come from URL params, NOT from `auth()->id()`. Attacker holding any sanctum token can hit `/admin/my-order/show/<bob_id>/<bob_order_id>` and receive Bob's order (with `transaction`, `orderItems`, `branch`, `user` eager-loaded). BranchScope on Order limits enumeration cross-branch (any staff branch_id>0 only resolves their branch's orders), but Admin (branch_id=0) bypass + any same-branch staff cross-user IDOR is open.
findings.exploit: Any authenticated staff member in branch X can enumerate {user_id, order_id} pairs of other customers in branch X. Admin users (branch_id=0) can enumerate cross-branch.
findings.callsite_inventory: Endpoint is ADMIN-ONLY (no frontend/account callsite). Consumers: resources/js/components/admin/customers/CustomerOrderDetailsComponent.vue, resources/js/components/admin/waiters/WaiterOrderDetailsComponent.vue, resources/js/components/admin/deliveryBoys/DeliveryBoyOrderDetailsComponent.vue — all via vuex action `myOrderDetails/orderDetails` (resources/js/store/modules/myOrderDetails.js L33). Frontend account/myOrder uses a different endpoint (not this one).
findings.fix_proposal_initial_REJECTED: Naive `auth()->id() === $user->id` would BREAK the 3 admin SPA flows that legitimately view OTHER users' orders (Customer/Waiter/DeliveryBoy detail views in admin). DO NOT apply.
findings.fix_proposal_recommended: Add `$this->middleware('permission:customers_show|waiters_show|delivery-boys_show')` (Spatie alternation OR) in MyOrderDetailsController constructor. This gates the 3 legitimate admin consumers and locks out non-staff tokens. Cleanest V1.0.2 design = split into 3 dedicated endpoints (/admin/customer/{user}/order/{order} gated by customers_show, /admin/waiter/... gated by waiters_show, /admin/delivery-boy/... gated by delivery-boys_show).
findings.heal_decision: DEFERRED to Round 2 / V1.0.2 — multi-consumer endpoint with permission alternation needs sentinel test (verify each role can still hit the legitimate view) before commit. Round 1 mandate says safe-heal only — this needs test infra first.

findings.title: MenuTemplateController CRUD ungated
findings.evidence: app/Http/Controllers/Admin/MenuTemplateController.php has no `permission:*` middleware (grep -n confirms). Routes `/admin/setting/menu-template` GET+POST+PUT+DELETE (routes/api.php L385-389) are inside `permission:settings` setting prefix group? Need to verify.
findings.verdict: VERIFIED — routes/api.php L295 opens `setting.` prefix group WITHOUT any group-level `permission:*` middleware. L384-390 declares menu-template inside this group. Group does NOT inherit a permission gate, so MenuTemplateController's lack of controller-level middleware leaves all 5 verbs ungated for any sanctum-auth token. P1 stands.
findings.heal_decision: DEFERRED to Round 2 — requires sentinel test (MenuTemplateAuthzTest) similar to PermissionControllerIndexAuthzTest. Round 1 mandate prefers test-backed heals.

findings.title: AnalyticController::index and show ungated
findings.evidence: app/Http/Controllers/Admin/AnalyticController.php L21: `$this->middleware(['permission:settings'])->only('store', 'update', 'destroy');` — `index` and `show` are NOT gated. Routes /admin/setting/analytic GET (L431) is inside `setting.` prefix group (verified L295 — group has NO permission middleware). Analytic stores tracking pixels / 3rd-party integration keys (GTM, FB Pixel, etc.).
findings.fix_proposal: Change `->only('store', 'update', 'destroy')` to no `only()` (gate all 5 methods) OR add `$this->middleware(['permission:settings'])->only('index', 'show')` line.

findings.title: FormRequest authz scattered — F-2 backlog known issue
findings.evidence: 96 FormRequest files. authorize() returns true by default in most — gating relies on route-level `permission:*` middleware. BRAIN notes F-2 backlog mentions 88 endpoints with scattered FormRequest authz. AdministratorRequest M-R3-P0-E heal is a positive example of correct FormRequest gating.
findings.verdict: Known V1.0.1 refactor target. Not a new finding. Not P0.

findings.title: ApiKey middleware uses config() (not env) — SEC-FIX confirmed
findings.evidence: ApiKeyMiddleware.php L20-21 comment: `// [SEC-FIX] Use config() not env() — env() returns null after php artisan config:cache`. Returns 400 on mismatch, not 401 (caller distinguishes auth-key from auth-user).

findings.title: M-R3-P0-A heal verified — PermissionController gated
findings.evidence: PermissionController.php L27-33 carries the heal comment and `$this->middleware(['permission:settings']);` covers all methods including `index`. Sentinel: PermissionControllerIndexAuthzTest.php exists.

findings.title: M-R3-P0-E heal verified — AdministratorRequest blocks branch_id=0 minting
findings.evidence: AdministratorRequest.php L74-91 withValidator after-rule. Non-superadmin caller submitting branch_id=0 receives 422 with R3 T-2.2.1 Sec S-3 message.

findings.title: CSRF — admin API routes don't use VerifyCsrfToken
findings.evidence: Admin routes live in routes/api.php which is `api` middleware group (no CSRF by default in Laravel — stateless via Sanctum tokens). Acceptable for token-based SPA architecture. Cookie-based session POSTs would need CSRF — not the case here.
findings.verdict: By design. Sanctum SPA mode auto-handles XSRF on /sanctum/csrf-cookie route. Not a finding.

findings.title: PaymentGatewayController.update — secrets storage check needed
findings.evidence: Not deeply audited in this pass (1500-word cap). PaymentGatewayController is gated `permission:settings`. Whether stored secrets (Stripe key etc.) are encrypted at rest (Laravel `encrypted` cast) requires migration + model review. Logged as deferred.

verdict: MIDDLEWARE STACK ACCEPTABLE. 1 P0 (S-1 MyOrderDetails IDOR), 2 P1 (S-2 MenuTemplate, S-3 Analytic read), 2 P2 deferred. 2 confirmed heals (M-R3-P0-A, M-R3-P0-E). The `apiKey` shared-secret pattern is conventional for FoodKing's deployment (single tenant key); not a finding.
